summary: SPAN destination LEAF-07 Gi1/0/48 is severely oversubscribed (2.06 Gbps mirrored into 1 Gbps) discarding 51.48% (7,957,500/15,457,440 packets) plus 3.56% loss on link to BROKER-A port 1. IDS receives only ~46.8% of intended traffic.

findings.root_cause: SPAN oversubscription and link loss: LEAF-07 Gi1/0/1 mirrors 15,457,440 packets (2.06 Gbps) but SPAN destination LEAF-07 Gi1/0/48 is only 1 Gbps and sent only 7,500,000 packets, discarding 7,957,500 on output (100% avg load, bursts higher) = 51.48% loss. Additional 3.56% loss between LEAF-07 Gi1/0/48 and BROKER-A port 1 (7,500,000 sent vs 7,233,300 received). SPAN cannot handle bursts and is fundamentally lossy when source exceeds destination.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions and full payload at 1 Gbps. Missing >51% of packets creates massive detection blind spot - attacks, exploits and C2 in dropped packets are invisible, state tracking fails, and IDS cannot reliably detect intrusions. Secondary 3.56% link loss adds further gaps.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy independent of switch CPU/buffer and destination port speed. Replace SPAN with physical TAP at LEAF-07 Gi1/0/1 feeding via packet broker with sufficient capacity/aggregation (2.06 Gbps+ headroom) to eliminate 51% SPAN drop. Also remediate link between LEAF-07 Gi1/0/48 and BROKER-A port 1 (check optics/cabling) to fix 3.56% transport loss.
